sources.title: BLS Standard Occupational Classification
sources.finding: Administrative/statistical structure: psychology and farm management do not sit where a casual browser necessarily expects. Retain codes as reference metadata, not the browsing tree.

sources.title: BLS: Psychologists
sources.finding: Distinguishes clinical/counseling, school, workplace, and other psychology work. Supports multiple discovery paths without assuming all psychology is therapy.

sources.title: BLS: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
sources.finding: Groups farm and ranch management; a game may offer differentiated scenarios while retaining a shared statistical reference.

sources.title: O*NET: Clinical and Counseling Psychologists
sources.finding: Reported titles help construct search vocabulary. Reported title lists do not establish credential equivalence between all listed professions.

sources.title: O*NET: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
sources.finding: Reported titles include ranch, greenhouse, and nursery management. This supports explicit cultivation and livestock subfamilies.

sources.title: O*NET: Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers
sources.finding: Groundskeeper and landscaper vocabulary overlaps; keep grounds discoverable from plant-related categories and facilities.

sources.title: OPM: Psychology Series 0180
sources.finding: Federal psychology has a distinct occupational series and professional requirements. Keep series and qualifications separate from player-facing category labels.

sources.title: IRS: 2025 Schedule C instructions and principal activity codes
sources.finding: Tax activity codes classify businesses. The list distinguishes mental-health practitioner offices from other physician offices and directs farming activity to Schedule F. Do not assign business activity codes as person-level occupation codes.

sources.title: Census: NAICS overview
sources.finding: NAICS classifies business establishments. Industry, employer sector, and occupation must remain separate relations.

sources.title: U.S. Army career browsing
sources.finding: Public career navigation exposes recognizable specialty routes such as medical, law, cyber, aviation, and bands. Parts of the job finder are client-rendered; no complete job taxonomy was extracted.

sources.title: U.S. Navy: Business, Logistics & Administration
sources.finding: Military recruiting also uses recognizable occupational groupings; service context should not hide transferable work.

sources.title: U.S. Navy: Clinical Psychology
sources.finding: A concrete military psychology route demonstrates overlap between medical, psychological, and service settings; it is not a substitute for the civilian role definition.

sources.title: O*NET military and other crosswalks
sources.finding: MOC and supplemental military linkages support many-to-many discovery. Similar duties do not automatically confer civilian credentials.

sources.title: SEEK: Psychology, Counselling & Social Work
sources.finding: A public browse family explicitly names psychology and counseling but nests it in healthcare. Supports both a prominent psychology entry and healthcare cross-links; not evidence that every board makes mental health top-level.

sources.title: SEEK: Farming, Animals & Conservation
sources.finding: Shows explicit horticulture and farm-labor subdivisions alongside animals and conservation. Supports separating recognizable work while preserving cross-links.

sources.title: Reed: job-search specialisms
sources.finding: Separately exposes IT, engineering, accounting, HR, manufacturing, social care, customer service, and other recognizable work categories. Supports splitting several overly broad current game branches.

sources.title: r/psychologystudents: counselor versus therapist
sources.finding: Illustrates confusion among professional labels and the ambiguity of therapist. Comments conflict about regulation; use only as language/problem evidence, not licensing authority.

sources.title: r/Horticulture: career path in horticulture
sources.finding: Illustrates searching across horticulture, landscaping, nursery work, growing, and forestry. One discussion is not a representative preference survey.

limitations: Forums illustrate vocabulary and confusion, not representative preferences or credential rules.
Job-board structures are design references, not proof of universal usability.
Military and civilian roles can overlap without sharing credentials.
Tax and NAICS categories describe business activities or establishments, not person-level occupations.
